title: Game On, Gym Rats — Late 90s/2000s Edition
description: A millennial-focused board covering the fitness fads and gym celebrities of the late 90s/early 2000s, iconic video games from that era that haven't been featured before, and breaking current events from 2025.

questions.question: This seven-time world karate champion from Erie, Pennsylvania launched his kickboxing-cardio VHS system in August 1998 — blending Tae Kwon Do and boxing — selling more than 1.5 million video sets and grossing over $80 million in his first year of national release.

Known for his bedazzled tank tops, rhinestone-studded short-shorts, and enthusiastic support of people struggling with their weight, this bubbly fitness personality hosted the 'Sweatin' to the Oldies' workout video series and operated a Beverly Hills exercise studio called Slimmons throughout the 1990s and 2000s.

Marketed relentlessly through late-night television infomercials in the late 1990s and early 2000s, this home gym system used flexible composite resistance rods instead of traditional iron plates, promising a complete strength workout without additional free weights — its distinctive bowed frame became one of the decade's most recognizable 'as seen on TV' fitness silhouettes.

Founded in Santa Cruz, California in 2000 by former gymnast Greg Glassman, this fitness methodology combined constantly varied functional movements — including Olympic lifting, gymnastics movements, and metabolic conditioning — performed at high intensity; while niche in its early years, it grew to over 15,000 affiliate gyms worldwide by the 2010s.

Bill Phillips's 1999 bestselling fitness book of the same name outlined a 12-week program pairing strength training with six small daily protein-rich meals; its companion transformation challenge — backed by his supplement company EAS — awarded a significant cash grand prize to contestants who submitted the most dramatic before-and-after photos.

First popularized by physician Robert Atkins in his 1972 book and revived in 1992, this dietary approach — dramatically restricting carbohydrates while allowing fat and protein in virtually unlimited quantities — surged again in the early 2000s, reportedly becoming the most followed diet in the United States.

This naturally occurring compound found in red meat and skeletal muscle became one of the most popular gym supplements of the late 1990s after peer-reviewed studies confirmed it improved explosive performance by helping muscles rapidly regenerate their primary energy molecule — ATP — during short, all-out efforts; it remains among the most extensively researched and widely used legal ergogenic aids.

Pioneered in Soviet sports science by Yuri Verkhoshansky and introduced to Western athletes in the 1970s, this training modality — characterized by explosive jumping, bounding, and box-leap drills designed to rapidly load and unload the stretch-shortening cycle — became a popular athletic conditioning tool in American gyms and high school sports programs throughout the 1990s.

Widely sold in late-1990s gyms and health food stores as a weight-loss and performance-boosting supplement, this stimulant compound — derived from the Chinese herb Ma Huang — was the FDA's most controversial dietary supplement of the era; the agency finally banned it in 2004 after it was linked to cardiovascular events including heart attacks and strokes.

Developed in 1981 by Dr. David Jenkins at the University of Toronto and published in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition, this nutritional scale ranks carbohydrates from 0 to 100 based on how quickly they raise blood glucose compared to pure glucose; it gained mainstream fitness attention in the late 1990s when athletes and diet book authors began using it to optimize nutrition and weight management.

First released in Japanese arcades on September 26, 1998 and reaching North American arcades in early 1999, this Konami rhythm game had players stomping their feet on directional arrows in sync with the music — pioneering the dance game genre and blurring the line between gaming and aerobic exercise.

This 1998 Capcom survival horror sequel placed rookie cop Leon S. Kennedy and college student Claire Redfield in zombie-overrun Raccoon City, where a unique 'Zapping System' gave each protagonist separate story paths, puzzles, and plot threads across four distinct playthroughs; it sold over six million copies on PlayStation alone.

Eidos Interactive's 1996 action-adventure series — starring a dual-pistol-wielding British aristocrat archaeologist who raided ancient ruins and solved environmental puzzles across five PlayStation adventures — established its protagonist as gaming's most iconic female hero of the late 1990s and later spawned two blockbuster films starring Angelina Jolie.

Blizzard's 2000 action RPG sequel expanded the world of its 1996 predecessor to five acts, introduced playable character classes including the Necromancer and Druid, and built out the Battle.net service for competitive online play — it became one of the best-selling PC games of its era and maintained an active player base for decades.

Konami's 1999 PlayStation horror title — set in a fog-shrouded American resort town where a father searches for his missing daughter — pioneered psychological horror by using the protagonist's fractured mind to distort the environment between a mundane real world and a rust-corroded nightmare called the Otherworld; composer Akira Yamaoka's unsettling industrial score became as celebrated as the game itself.

Congressional hearings in 1993 and 1994 — spurred by the brutal fatality system of this Midway fighting game, which allowed players to decapitate opponents and rip out their spines — led directly to the creation of the Entertainment Software Rating Board, the voluntary content rating system that still appears on video game packaging today.

Released for the Nintendo 64 in April 2000 and developed in just over a year by director Eiji Aonuma, this direct Zelda sequel gave players only three in-game days before a falling moon would destroy the world — requiring constant time resets through a magical ocarina; its dark, melancholy tone divided fans while earning widespread critical acclaim.

questions.question: Launched in March 1999 by Verant Interactive, this fantasy online role-playing game — set in the persistent world of Norrath and offering multiple character races and classes — became so addictive that gaming press nicknamed it 'EverCrack'; it laid the commercial and design foundation for the massively multiplayer online genre that World of Warcraft would later dominate.

Originally created as a free Half-Life modification in June 1999 by Minh 'Gooseman' Le and Jess Cliffe — pitting a counter-terrorist team against terrorists in competitive elimination rounds — this tactical first-person shooter became so popular that Valve acquired it in 2000 and released it commercially; it went on to become one of the most-played competitive PC games in history.

Smilebit's 1999 Sega Dreamcast exclusive — a cel-shaded urban skating game set in a fictionalized Tokyo where rival roller-blading gangs competed through graffiti art to an eclectic funk-hip-hop soundtrack — is remembered as gaming's earliest major showcase of cel-shaded 3D graphics and remains a cult touchstone of early 2000s game design.

On April 21, 2025, this 88-year-old Argentine-born leader of the Roman Catholic Church died after suffering a stroke — he had served as pope since 2013, taken his name from the saint of Assisi, and was the first Latin American to lead the Church in its history.

On May 8, 2025, this Chicago-born Augustinian cardinal — who held dual U.S. and Peruvian citizenship after years of missionary work in northern Peru — was elected the 267th pope on the fourth ballot of the conclave, becoming the first American pontiff in the Catholic Church's 2,000-year history.

At the 97th Academy Awards ceremony on March 2, 2025, this Sean Baker-directed film about a New York sex worker who hastily marries into a Russian oligarch's family won five awards including Best Picture and Best Actress for Mikey Madison — Baker's four personal wins (Picture, Director, Screenplay, Editing) tied Walt Disney's record for most Oscars in a single ceremony.

In May 2025, India launched military strikes it described as targeting 'terrorist infrastructure' across the border following an attack that killed 26 people near Pahalgam — this nuclear-armed neighbor responded with drone and missile strikes against Indian military bases before both sides agreed to a ceasefire after three days of their most intense fighting in half a century.

At Berkshire Hathaway's annual shareholder meeting on May 3, 2025, this 94-year-old Nebraska native — widely called the 'Oracle of Omaha' — announced he would step down as CEO at year's end after nearly six decades running the conglomerate he had built into one of the world's largest companies; Greg Abel was named as his successor pending board approval.

Beginning in early 2025, the Trump administration imposed sweeping tariffs on goods from this Asian economic superpower — triggering a retaliatory trade war that included new export controls on rare earth minerals critical to American technology manufacturing and sent global stock markets into significant volatility.

On April 28, 2025, Canada held a federal election in which this former governor of both the Bank of Canada and the Bank of England led his Liberal Party to defeat Pierre Poilievre's Conservatives, becoming prime minister after Justin Trudeau's earlier resignation amid a political crisis.

On March 2, 2025, this Texas-based private aerospace company made history when its Blue Ghost lander successfully touched down on the Moon's surface to deliver NASA science payloads to the Mare Crisium region — becoming the first commercial company to achieve a successful lunar landing under NASA's Commercial Lunar Payload Services program.

On March 28, 2025, a 7.7 magnitude earthquake struck this Southeast Asian nation — causing over 5,400 deaths and widespread structural collapse — making it one of the deadliest seismic disasters in the region in years; the military government controlling the country faced international criticism for its coordination of relief efforts.

On February 23, 2025, voters in this central European nation went to the polls in a snap federal election — triggered by a coalition government collapse — where Friedrich Merz's center-right CDU/CSU bloc won the most seats, while the far-right Alternative für Deutschland simultaneously notched its best-ever national result with 20.8% of the vote; the country's domestic intelligence office later declared the party a right-wing extremist organization.
